# Register — ZenPom

**THIS FILE IS HAND-MAINTAINED IN THIS REPOSITORY. Nothing here regenerates it.**
It is the register `docs/conventions.md` Axis 2 describes: one `##` per register, every row carrying a
status, every register sorted by ID, every ID appearing exactly once. It is **read** by
`scripts/gen_status.py`, which writes `docs/plans/00-status.md` from it and never writes back.

**PROVENANCE, CORRECTED 2026-09-23 by `C33`.** This header previously read *"Regenerated by
`scripts/extract_zenpom.py`, which MERGES"*, and described a `Mode`/`TD` merge protocol for an
extractor that **exists in no branch and no commit of this repository** (`docs/chores/C28.md:32`;
`docs/plans/F13.md:663` records the upstream tool as carrying `O`, `D` and `C` only, so it has never
heard of `A`, `M`, `H` or `RR`). The `Mode` and `TD` columns are real and are kept — `TD` holds the
Todoist links the owner's own sync uses — but no run refreshes them and an empty cell asks for
nothing. **This is `docs/conventions.md`'s validate-every-artefact case** — cited by name and not by
its upstream decision number, because that number is an upstream one and this project's delta walk
(`H1`) rightly refuses a `D<n>` with no heading in `docs/plans/00-deltas.md`, which stops at `D41`:
the tables below were checked row by row and the sentence describing where they come from was not
read.

**EIGHT OF THE 26 ROWS BELOW CARRY THE LITERAL VALUE `unknown` IN `Status`** — `C9`, `C10`, `C12`,
`C14`, `C16`, `C18`, `C19`, `C20`. The other eighteen carry `closed` (14) or `open` (4). The eight are
what an extractor with no status to copy wrote down, and they are left for the owner to rule on rather
than guessed at: establishing each would mean reading that chore's own file and git history, which is
research and not transcription.

**THIS PARAGRAPH READ *"No chore in ZenPom carries a status field. Every row below is `unknown`"*
UNTIL 2026-09-23,** when `C33`'s adversarial review caught it. It was false for 18 of 26 rows — and
the same diff that added `closed`/`open` to `C1`, `C13`, `C15`, `C21`, `C23` and `C24` added them
directly beneath the two lines saying no such row existed, without reading them. **`docs/conventions.md`
Axis 2's mandatory field is PRESENT on all 26 rows; on eight of them its VALUE is outside any pinned
vocabulary,** which is a different defect and needs a different check — see the note under the table.

**`unknown` IS A VALUE HERE AND IT IS ALSO WHAT AN EMPTY CELL BECOMES.** `scripts/gen_status.py:174`
maps an absent `Status` to the string `unknown` as well, so `docs/plans/00-status.md`'s
`| Chores (C) | 26 | 4 | 8 | 14 |` **cannot distinguish a row that says `unknown` from a row that says
nothing.** Today every one of the eight is the first kind; no chore row has an empty cell. A `C34`
check written to fire on an empty status cell would therefore fire on **zero** of the eight rows it was
written for. The check these rows need is **enum membership** — `Status` must be one of a pinned
vocabulary, and `unknown` is not in it — which is `C33.md`'s row shape 14.

**Status is derived, and the derivation is mechanical so it can be checked rather than taken:**

nothing else: `gen_status.py`'s closed set is fixed, so a nuanced word would count silently as open.

it is not contemporaneous, and the owner may overrule it.** Closed rows are left blank, because a
priority on a closed row is noise. If the owner would rather an agent register carried no priorities
at all, blank all nineteen — the register stays valid, because `P` is not the field

after `C33`'s adversarial review. `P2` is the floor, so *seen once, never reproduced* and *real,

## Mutations (M)

**Opened 2026-09-23 by `C33`, implementing `D38`, with full backfill.** 103 rows: every mutation ID
in use anywhere in this project. **`C33` re-runs none of them** — the register records which were run
and when, rather than implying this chore re-verified them.

**`Title` is the mutation description.** `D38` proposed the column name `Mutation`;
`scripts/gen_status.py` keys a row's fields off the table's own lowercased headers and reads `title`,
so `Mutation` would render blank everywhere. The divergence is recorded rather than left looking like
a mistake. `P` is empty throughout: a mutation is run or it is not, and a priority on it means nothing.

**`Run` IS THE COLUMN THAT MATTERS, and it is a pinned enum of three values.** It separates the **61
mutations that have been applied to shipped code — 60 `run` and one `escaped` — from the 42 that have
never touched code.** `run` — applied to shipped code, the named test seen to go red, then restored.
`escaped` — applied, and the named test did **not** catch it; this project has exactly one, `F8-M9`,
and flattening it into `run` would be the lie the column exists to prevent. `proposed` — named in a
plan for work that has not been built.

**SO 61 IS NOT THE COUNT OF MUTATIONS *SEEN TO FAIL*, AND THIS PARAGRAPH SAID IT WAS UNTIL
2026-09-23,** when `C33`'s adversarial review caught it: the sentence read *"the 61 mutations that have
been seen to fail"* four lines above the sentence pinning `escaped` as the case where the named test
did not catch it, which is the flattening the column exists to prevent, performed silently by the
paragraph that forbids it. **Seen to fail is 60.** `escaped` is the sixty-first application and its
own row says the first application escaped. `docs/plans/00-status.md`'s `| Mutations (M) | 103 | 42 |
0 | 61 |` is a **`Status`** count, not a `Run` count — `F8-M9`'s `Status` is `closed` because it was
caught after the fixture and the regex were repaired — and reading that 61 back as a `Run` figure is
how the two got conflated. **Both numbers are derivable from the table below and neither is asserted
here:**

```
python3 - <<'PY'
import re, collections
sec = re.search(r'## Mutations \(M\)\n(.*?)\n## ', open('docs/plans/00-register.md').read(), re.S).group(1)
rows = [l for l in sec.split('\n') if l.startswith('| ') and not l.startswith(('|---', '| ID '))]
run = collections.Counter(l.strip().strip('|').split('|')[4].strip() for l in rows)
print(len(rows), run)          # 103 Counter({'run': 60, 'proposed': 42, 'escaped': 1})
PY
```

**A FOURTH VALUE, `run, no count`, WAS PINNED AND IS WITHDRAWN 2026-09-23 after `C33`'s adversarial
review: zero of the 103 rows used it.** A pinned enum with a dead member is an invitation — the next
writer who has no suite count reaches for the value that sounds like their situation instead of for
`escaped` or a real number. The distinction it was for is already carried by the `Count` column, which
reads `—` on 48 rows and means exactly *run, and no count was recorded at the time*. One fact, one
column.
**A mutation is `run` only where a source records it FAILING.** *"Named now and run before this task
is called done"* (`docs/plans/F8.md:468`) is a promise, and a promise filed as a run makes this
register the false-assurance instrument `docs/conventions.md` describes at length.

**TWO SPELLINGS, AND THEY ARE NOT TWO NAMES FOR ONE POPULATION.** Bare `M1`–`M20`, `M22`, `M23` are
genuine project-global IDs from the `F4` retrofit series and `C12`. The rest are scoped to the unit
that owns them, which is what `docs/conventions.md` asks for. They coexist. **`M21` and `M24`–`M33`
are gaps: legal, permanent, and never closed by renumbering** (`D17`).

**THE COUNTS WERE RE-DERIVED AND `D38`'s HAVE MOVED.**
`grep -rhoE '\b[FC][0-9]+[a-z]*-M[0-9]+[a-z]*' . --exclude-dir=.git | sort -u | wc -l` returns 74
scoped IDs present in the tree at `bc4e0f2`; `D38`'s own `F`-only command returns 58 against the 52 it
recorded, the difference being `F7b`, and it cannot see `C28`'s three or `C32`'s thirteen at all. Add
three `F8` IDs that exist only in a commit body and four of `C33`'s own, and the scoped population is
81; with the 22 bare that is **103**. (`C33-M4` was allocated after the adversarial review, against the
one further line of `gen_status.py` that review asked for; 102 is the figure before it.)

**`M34` IS NOT AN ALLOCATED ID AND HAS NO ROW HERE.** Its only two appearances in the tree are denials
of its own existence: `docs/plans/F15.md:445` — *"The draft claimed `M34` was the highest in the
register; it is not"*, the number having come from a Todoist task id on the `O23` row — and `D38`'s
own enumeration line, which took the draft's word. **`D38`'s `(M1–M20, M22, M23, M34)` overcounts by
one. The delta's text is not edited; the correction lives here.**

**FIVE IDS ARE DEFINED ONLY IN A COMMIT BODY** — `F8-M6`, `F8-M10`, `F8-M11`, `F8-M12`, `F8-M13` — and
each says so in its own cell. The class is filed once as `A19` rather than as five rows of the same
complaint. **The cells are a TRANSCRIPTION of that commit body and not a source**: the definition is
stated here, in a file, and is still traceable only by leaving the tree, which is the distinction
`A19` is about.

**AND THREE OF THOSE ROWS — `F8-M11`, `F8-M12`, `F8-M13` — NAME NO TEST AT ALL.** Their
`Test that catches it` reads `not named in the source`, because the commit body records a count of
tests going red and no test name. `docs/conventions.md` defines a mutation as *"named ways to break the
code, each paired with the test that must catch it"*, so a row that is `run` with no citable test is
**a second, distinct row shape from `A19`'s** — the source is unreachable in `A19`'s case and simply
absent in this one — and a `C34` check on `A19`'s shape passes all three of these. It is
`docs/chores/C33.md`'s row shape 15, added 2026-09-23 after `C33`'s second review pass found it missing
from the fourteen. Not repaired here: inventing a test name for a mutation run three weeks ago in
another unit would be the reconstruction this register refuses.

**`F8-M7` AND `F8-M8` EACH NAME TWO DIFFERENT MUTATIONS.** That is `O43`, it is the owner's to rule
on, and this chore writes **one row per ID** with the collision stated. No disambiguating suffix is
allocated, because `F8-M7a` would be an identifier nothing cites.

**SORTING. THE SOURCE IS IN ID ORDER, AND THE ORDER IS A STATED KEY.** `docs/conventions.md`,
Axis 2: *every register is sorted by ID*, for a writer's reason — *allocating the next number must
not require scanning forty unsorted rows.* The key is the ID parsed as
`(prefix, number, retrofit letter, scoped prefix, scoped number, scoped letter)`, which gives
`C28` · `C32` · `C33` · `F7b` · `F8` · `F10` · `F14`–`F19` · `M1`–`M23`, and it puts the highest
`F8` mutation immediately above `F10-M1` instead of eighty rows away. **An earlier draft of this
section sorted the source to match `gen_status.py`'s output**, which is backwards:
`docs/conventions.md` says *"re-sorting for reading is the generated status page's job, not the
source's."* The page's own `sort_key` does not parse a scoped id and degrades to `(unit_id, 0, "")`,
so the page prints an order of its own. That divergence is the page's business and no longer the
source's. The 103 rows were re-sorted with no content change, proved by diffing the
`(ID, first 40 characters of Title)` pairs before and after — identical, as `C29`'s procedure
requires.

## Hooks (H)

**Opened 2026-09-23 by `C33`, implementing `D38`, with full backfill.** Traced *spec invariant →
mechanism → owning unit*, which are the `Invariant`, `Mechanism` and `Owning unit` columns.
`Title` is the hook's short name and exists because `scripts/gen_status.py` prints `h.get('title')`
under a column it labels `Hook`.

**THE COUNT IS THIRTY-ONE IN-TREE MECHANISMS, AND IT IS NOT FIFTEEN.** `D38` refused to inherit
`docs/handoffs/blockersfor1_5.md:71`'s *"15 real enforcement mechanisms"* because no command had been
shown to reproduce it, and made establishing the real count the first work of this chore. **A
mechanism is a check that (a) is invoked by a named command, (b) can FAIL and thereby stop a commit, a
CI run or a test run, and (c) defends a stated spec invariant or a ratified decision rather than a
formatting preference. It is counted ONCE AT ITS DEFINITION SITE, never once per surface that invokes
it** — `scripts/check-secrets.sh` runs at pre-commit and in CI and is one row with two values in
`Runs at`. Counting invocations instead of definitions is how a count inflates without anything being
built. The enumerating command, the twelve/one/seventeen breakdown, and the exclusions — which are the
argument, and the criterion by which a Swift suite is a mechanism — are in `docs/chores/C33.md`.
**It was thirty until this register was reviewed.** The enumeration's Swift half was a hand-written
`ls` of seventeen named files, so it reproduced its own answer instead of deriving it, and it missed
`ZenTomatoTests/TodoistEndpointTests.swift` — which defends the project's loudest non-negotiable and
meets every part of the criterion. That is `H32`, added after review. **The tree was not touched to
reach any number.** Fifteen was
not reproducible under any defensible rule; the near misses are ten `scripts/check-*.sh` excluding
`install-device`, twelve shell/Python checks, sixteen CI steps including setup, and seven hook
invocations, and it matches none of them.

**THE TABLE HAS 32 ROWS AGAINST 31 IN-TREE MECHANISMS.** The extra is `H31`, GitHub branch protection:
real, named in `CLAUDE.md`'s hook table, and outside this repository, so no command here reproduces
it. Leaving it out would make the register disagree with `CLAUDE.md`; writing it `closed` would be the
confident-sentence failure `docs/conventions.md` names.

**ALLOCATION ORDER, so the next allocator does not have to guess and the allocation is reproducible:**
`H1`, `H2` and `H3` keep the meanings `docs/chores/C6.md` fixed for them; then the remaining
shell/Python checks in `ls scripts/check-*.sh` order, then `gen_status.py`, then
`run-script-tests.sh`, then the SwiftLint custom rule, then the Swift contract/fence suites in `ls`
order, then `H31`. **`H32` is out of that order**, allocated after the adversarial review found a
mechanism the `ls` line had missed; an ID is an identifier and not an index, so the table is not
renumbered to close the seam (`D17`).

**`Proved by: never` IS THE HONEST AND COMMON ANSWER — nineteen of thirty-two — AND IT IS THE POINT
OF THE COLUMN.** A mechanism that exists but has never been broken to watch it fail is `open`, not
`closed`: *a hook that has never failed is a hook nobody knows works.* **THIRTEEN ROWS ARE `closed`
AND EVERY ONE OF THEM NAMES THE MUTATION THAT PROVED IT.** The count is derivable from the table and
is not asserted here: `Status: closed` and a `Proved by` cell containing the word `never` cannot both
be true of one row, and no row satisfies both.

**FOUR ROWS SHIPPED VIOLATING THAT RULE AND WERE CORRECTED 2026-09-23 by `C33`'s adversarial
review.** `H5`, `H7`, `H15` and `H30` were written `closed` beside `Proved by: never` — `H5`'s own
`Why` said *"Nothing has ever broken this script to watch it fail"* next to the word `closed` — and
the preamble's own tally said sixteen where the table held eighteen, missing exactly two of the four.
**The miscount and the wrong statuses were the same error twice**, and the generated page carried it:
`docs/plans/00-status.md` published *"17 of 31 built"* where the register's own derivation gives
thirteen. Each of the four carries the correction in its `Why` rather than being quietly reset.

`Owning unit` is read out of
`git log --oneline --diff-filter=A` on the mechanism's own file, so two rows record a scope that is
wrong rather than a scope that should have been right.

**THREE MECHANISMS ARE WIRED TO NOTHING** — `H6`, `H10` and `H12`. They appear in no hook, no CI step
and no `make` target; `grep -rl` for their names hits only documentation and themselves. `Runs at` is
`manual` and `Status` is `open`, because a hook register that reported protection this project does
not have would be worse than no register.

**`Invariant` is sourced, never composed.** It comes from `CLAUDE.md`'s hook table where that names
one, from the script's own header comment otherwise, and from the suite's `///` docblock for the Swift
fences. Where no invariant could be sourced the cell would read `unsourced`; none did.

## Risks (RR)

**Opened 2026-09-23 by `C33`, implementing `D38`. These are SEEDS, not a backfill.** `RR` has no
backlog to recover, and `D38` says in as many words that seeds are honest where a backfill would be
invention. **Each of the four carries a file and a line.** A fifth was looked for and refused:
TestFlight timing, App Store review and the hard stop are real but are evidenced nowhere citable, and
the rule about a claim recorded before it is verified applies to a risk row as much as to anything
else.

**`Likelihood` IS FILLED ON ALL FOUR ROWS, AND THREE OF THE FOUR ARE NOT PROBABILITIES.** The column
shipped as `—` on 4 of 4 rows and was filled 2026-09-23 after `C33`'s adversarial review pointed out
that `docs/conventions.md` defines this register by exactly five contents — *risk, likelihood, impact,
mitigation, owner* — and the one being opened was empty on its defining field, which a validator
cannot tell from *not applicable*.

**It is deliberately not a pinned `low`/`medium`/`high` enum.** Two of these risks have no probability
to state and pinning three words would have forced an invention: `RR1` cannot occur at all while the
v1.5 scope holds, and `RR4` has already occurred. So the cell says which kind of statement it is
making, and every row's `Evidence` carries the sentence behind it. `certain — already happened`
(`RR4`) is an **observation**: the harm is in the data now. `none while v1.5 holds` (`RR1`) is
**structural**: there is no mechanism by which it can occur until a delta admits one. Anything else
(`RR2`, `RR3`) is **an assessment made by the agent on 2026-09-23, not a measurement, and the owner may
overrule it** — the same standing as the `A` register's priorities, and stated rather than dressed as
contemporaneous.

**The vocabulary is written as prose and NOT as a second markdown table, and that is not a style
choice.** `scripts/gen_status.py`'s `parse_tables` takes a section's field names from the **first**
table it meets in that section and never resets them, so a `| Value | Means |` legend placed above the
`RR` table would have made every risk row parse under the headers `value` and `means`, lose its `id`,
and vanish from a page CI keeps current — **four rows silently, on the day the register opens**. The
draft of this paragraph did exactly that and was caught by generating the page. It is `C34`'s row shape
13.

| ID | Title | P | Status | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation | Owner | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RR1 | iCloud/CloudKit sync would put the log where a conflict can lose it | P0 | open | none while v1.5 holds | the crown jewel | none today; the risk is the scope decision itself | owner | `docs/specs/zenpom-v1.5.md:185`, verbatim: *"A platform, and **the highest-risk item on either list.** The log is local-only today with no conflict resolution to get wrong. Sync is where the crown jewel would be lost."* The project's own words for its worst case. **Likelihood is `none while v1.5 holds` and not a probability**: sync is not in the v1.5 scope, so there is no mechanism by which this can occur until a delta admits one. The row exists so that delta meets the risk already written down. |
| RR2 | Changing the bundle identifier orphans the SwiftData store holding the distraction log | P0 | open | low, and conditional | total loss of the data `O1` needs | `C26`'s standing DO NOT | owner | `docs/chores/C26.md:25-33`: *"A bundle identifier is not a name, it is an identity, and changing it makes a different app"* / *"Changing the bundle identifier would destroy the data O1 needs before O1 has ever been run."* The App Store rejected the name `ZenTomato`, which is what makes this live rather than theoretical. **Likelihood assessed 2026-09-23 by `C33`, not measured**: the trigger is a deliberate human edit to one Xcode setting, guarded by `C26`’s standing DO NOT and by `O1`’s dependence on the store — low, but it is the App Store rejection that keeps it non-zero. |
| RR3 | The shape cursor and `TimerState` advance non-atomically, and control flow now derives from the seam | P1 | open | low per kill, unbounded over time | a lost block, or a sprint ending one block early | none | agent | `docs/reviews/F8.md:137-140`: *"the shape cursor (UserDefaults) and TimerState (SwiftData) advance non-atomically, so a process kill between advanceShape() and persist() loses a block. Pre-existing — but 2fab614 now derives control flow from it."* One row, not two: the sibling defect two lines up — `shapeJustSpent` derived from two separate `UserDefaults` reads either side of `advanceShape()`, where a failed decode ends the sprint a block early — is the same seam. **Likelihood assessed 2026-09-23 by `C33`, not measured**: the window is the microseconds between `advanceShape()` and `persist()`, so any single process kill is unlikely to land in it, but `F8` is halted at `T3` with no mitigation, so the exposure accumulates for as long as that holds. No measurement exists and none is claimed. |

The owner: *"tapping the app in the watch has a long delay — more than 2 seconds — and it led to an excessive number of I and E clicks."* The lag is fixed; the data is not: *"The taps already made are real rows and are still in the database. There is no capture surface and no editor, by design, so nothing in the app can remove them. Any export covering that block will over-report."* **Likelihood is `certain — already happened`, not a forecast**: the inflating rows are in the database now, by the owner’s own report, and there is no capture surface and no editor to remove them. This is the one RR row whose likelihood is an observation rather than an assessment. |

## Defect — reused IDs

Each ID below names **two or more different rows** in `OPEN.md`. The
tally beside it is counted from the source, not asserted. All-closed is
a naming collision only; **two open rows is a sync defect**, because
one `td:` id cannot link two rows and the register cannot tell them
apart. `D17` forbids renumbering to close a *gap*; a *collision* is the
opposite case and needs the owner's ruling on which one gets a new
number.

- `O23` — 1 closed, 1 open
- `O24` — 2 closed, 0 open
- `O25` — 1 closed, 1 open
